content:
**memory verbs reach a working backend (#641)**

memory:save was pinned to plainfiles by REQ-530-1; share/pull/index were not, so the verb the PR template names hard-failed wherever engram is absent while MEMORY_BACKEND=plainfiles worked the whole time. Measured on main@1c21976: memory:share exit 1, plainfiles exit 0 and delivering #574's duplicate report the documented verb could not reach. Ruling: fall back at the dispatcher (ADR-0004 owns the selector) on three conditions -- backend not stated, binary measurably absent via a DIRECT probe never a caught error message, and the op is one plainfiles serves natively -- and announce the substitution on stderr. A stated MEMORY_BACKEND is never overridden; its failure now names the working route instead of only an install command. The probe is three-valued: spawnSync reports its own failure in .error while leaving status null, so the old two-valued test read a broken probe as a confident absence -- evidence-reader-empty-on-failure, harmless as an error string but not once that same answer decides whether to switch a backend. requireEngram now reads the same probe, so no second copy of 'which engram' can drift. Found while measuring and NOT fixed: memory:index with no engram exits 0 reporting '0 documentos indexados' after failing on every document.
